q: Is it private? I don't want my editor sending data anywhere.
a: The only thing Revolution sends on its own is the daily update check: one request to GitHub (api.github.com) asking for the newest release of this build's line. GitHub sees your IP address, as with any web page; no usage data, names or identifiers are sent. If you'd rather it didn't, untick **Check for updates every day** in Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ **Updates**, or choose **Don't check for updates** the first time the window opens.

q: Will a slow connection make Revolution freeze when it looks for updates?
a: No. The check runs in the background, so a slow or missing connection never stalls Revolution. If GitHub doesn't answer (offline, rate-limited, a broken reply) it just tries again the next day and shows nothing.

q: What's the quickest way to install a new Revolution build when the corner window says one is out?
a: Click **Update** (`app.update.install`). Revolution downloads the build, checks it against the release's `SHA256SUMS`, and unpacks it into its own folder beside the one you are running; you can keep editing while a bar shows the progress. When it says **Installed**, click **Restart Now**, or keep working: the next time you start Revolution from its launcher, the new build opens. The release notes in the window help you decide whether now is a good time, and **Later** just closes it.

q: Why is clicking Update safe even on a deadline?
a: Four reasons: the download is checked against the release's published checksums (`SHA256SUMS`), so a damaged or tampered file is refused; the new build goes into its own folder, and only when everything is in place does Revolution switch the launcher's `latest` link to it, in one step; if anything fails or the download is interrupted, the build you are running stays as it was and half-finished downloads are removed; and the previous build is kept, so you can roll back. If you're mid-job, **Later** is still a fine answer: nothing installs until you choose.

q: What happens when I choose Later on the update popup?
a: **Later** just closes the **Update available** window. The next day's check asks again only if an even newer build has appeared. You can still install that build any time from Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ **Updates** with **Check Now**.

q: I turned off update checks. How do I look for a new build by hand?
a: Open Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ **Updates** (`app.settings.update`) and click **Check Now** (`app.update.check`). It asks GitHub right away even when the daily check is off; the line above it says what it found: up to date, an update, or why it didn't get an answer. Tick **Check for updates every day** again if you want the automatic check back.

q: Resolve has a 'check for updates' tickbox in its preferences. Is there an equivalent?
a: Yes: Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ **Updates** (`app.settings.update`) has **Check for updates every day**, on by default, plus **Check Now**. The difference from Resolve: Revolution also checks once a day while running, not only at start, and shows an **Update available** window in the bottom-right corner when it finds something.

q: Where's the update button? My copy only shows a link to the release page.
a: That copy of Revolution wasn't installed by the build procedure (for example a Flatpak, a distribution package or a build run from a source folder), so the window offers **Open the Release Page** instead of **Update** and says why. Builds packaged by someone else are updated by their packager's own updater.

q: An update introduced a bug for me. How do I get the old Revolution back?
a: Open Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ **Updates** and click **Roll Back to …** (`app.update.rollback`); it names the build the update replaced. The launcher points back at that build and the next start opens it. The newer build stays in its folder, so the next check offers it again: choose **Later** or untick the daily check until a fixed build is out.

q: Can an agent update Revolution without clicking through the window?
a: Yes, through `app.update.*`: `app.update.check` looks for a newer release, `app.update.status` reports what was found, `app.update.install` downloads, checks and installs it beside the running build, `app.update.rollback` goes back to the build it replaced, and `app.update.setEnabled` (`"enabled": false`) turns the daily check off. `command.list` shows their parameters.

context.q: An Update available window appeared. Should I click Update?
context.a: Read the release notes in the window first. **Update** downloads the build, checks it against `SHA256SUMS` and installs it beside the one you are running, so you can keep working; **Later** closes the window.

q: ok it says installed now, what next
a: Click **Restart Now**: Revolution closes as usual, asking about unsaved work first, and starts the new build. Or keep working and restart when it suits you: the next start from the launcher opens the new build.

context.q: How do I go back to the build before the update?
context.a: Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ **Updates** ▸ **Roll Back to …**. The launcher points back at the previous build; the next start opens it.

q: is the newer one deleted then
a: No. The newer build stays in its folder, which is also why the next daily check offers it again. Choose **Later** when it does, or untick **Check for updates every day** while you wait for a fix.
